feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/communications CV with credible scope, clear public-sector positioning, and good evidence of leadership across platforms, governance, analytics, and multimedia. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense, slightly repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by prioritizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary establish a coherent niche in digital platform leadership for complex, mission-driven organizations.  
- Strong credibility: NACo progression shows sustained advancement, and the website migration, analytics stack, and studio build-out add concrete scale.  
- Broad but relevant skill set: technical, editorial, analytics, and multimedia capabilities are well aligned to the target leadership profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve scannability and save space.  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe duties well, but more results would strengthen impact (e.g., engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption rates, campaign performance).  
- Tighten style consistency: use parallel bullet phrasing throughout, and standardize punctuation around lists and compounds. Minor style issues include “social, and multimedia” (remove comma), possible overuse of “organization’s,” and mixed formatting such as “A2/Learning” vs more standard “A2 (learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It would be sharper with one concrete scale signal and slightly less overlap with the subtitle, competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing: “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” is wordy; simplify to “leading” or “building and scaling.”
- Add one proof point from recent experience to increase impact, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Replace the generic “complex, mission-driven organizations” with “public-sector and membership organizations” for specificity.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector and membership-organization communications. Leads enterprise web transformation, digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search/content experiences—most recently directing a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; consider using the intro for differentiation via scale/results instead.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” is broad and repeats skills/projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is more specific and aligned with the CV.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, executive-level wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, dashboards, and reporting.”
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Multi-channel digital communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Consider sharpening “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for clarity.
- Suggested version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel digital communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific language already covered elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple role bullets; retain only if targeting public-sector or association roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a closing section. Tightening wording and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in and use parallel verb-led phrasing for consistency: “Selected recent projects include…”
- Tighten each item and foreground the differentiator: AI search, Drupal 10 microsite, anniversary campaign, recurring video series.
- Standardize style and hyphenation: “AI-enabled,” “bill-level,” “10 x 20-foot,” and consistent comma use.
- Consider this rewrite: “Selected recent projects: **AI Hybrid Search** — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat. **We Are Counties Microsite** — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and scalable modular architecture. **Organization Anniversary Campaign** — Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. **Advocacy Video Series** — Produced a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI search, microsite development, and advocacy video work closely overlap with current and NACo roles; keep only if this footer is meant as a concise “selected projects” highlight.
- “Built/developed” repeats frequently across the CV; vary with “designed,” “launched,” “produced,” or “delivered.”

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but the bullets are too task-heavy and overlap with the header, skills, and project section. Tighten around 3–4 high-impact outcomes and make the freelance/full-time nature feel more like a senior embedded engagement.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope line: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “led,” “built,” “designed,” “streamlined,” “launched.”
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Led enterprise web and communications improvements across Drupal, analytics, and editorial workflows to strengthen cross-channel coordination.
- Built campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits within Drupal.
- Improved CMS/front-end operations for public-facing web properties, including troubleshooting, usability, and governance.
- Shaped an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing time reduced, toolkit downloads, search success, or workflow efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/editorial systems also repeat the header and NACo role—avoid restating them in full.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening line were less list-like and if channel oversight bullets emphasized outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the intro with a tighter impact summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, multi-channel distribution, analytics, governance, and budget oversight across web, email, social, and video.”
- Tighten and front-load the biggest win: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-oriented; if possible add growth/open-rate/engagement metrics: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials, strengthening advocacy and member communications.”
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built analytics and governance infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video production and newsletter management overlap with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems-building.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” also appears elsewhere; use stronger senior-level wording here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as support-oriented rather than outcome-driven. Emphasize scope, channel ownership, and systems/process impact while avoiding claims already covered more strongly in the later director role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points; e.g.:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video series, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built cross-functional editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve coordination and publishing consistency.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to increase efficiency and content quality.
- Add metrics if available: email open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, turnaround-time improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and footer project.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version more execution-focused.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level leadership themes and avoid generic phrasing like “audience-focused content planning.”

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and communications operations
- Editorial governance and scalable content systems
- Cross-channel leadership for web, email, social and video
- Public-sector and advocacy communications strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for a more senior phrase such as “content operations and campaign planning” or “organization-wide editorial planning.”
- Keep wording aligned with recent impact: governance, enterprise web modernization, and cross-channel operations are better supported by 2022–present roles than broad “messaging” language.
- If space allows, make one bullet outcome-oriented: “Digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms and campaigns.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with the header and multiple NACo roles; “communications strategy” is stronger and less repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads as a tool dump rather than a senior, impact-oriented skills summary. In this topline section, emphasize current platforms and modernization strengths over older/commodity tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from list of tools to grouped capabilities tied to recent work:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- SharePoint, Power Pages and Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search and content experiences
- Drop “jQuery” here unless it is central to target roles; it feels dated for a topline skills section.
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress only if relevant to target jobs; recent experience is clearly Drupal-led.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep topline skills higher-level and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies—avoid repeating exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic capability and decision-making, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting”
- Group tools as enablers, not the headline: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten phrasing and elevate seniority: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and decision support”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave the full tool stack there.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; consider folding it into “UX and performance analysis.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps with “Core Competencies” and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership + delivery: “Broadcast-quality studio operations • Livestream and hybrid event production • PTZ camera systems • Video production workflows • Virtual event delivery”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to sound more senior.
- If space allows, add scale/setting language: “for advocacy, conference, and member-facing programming.”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools (“PTZ camera systems”) with broad functions unless all bullets are similarly scoped.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- Studio/video capability is already evidenced in NACo experience, so this skills item should summarize, not restate those accomplishments.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. In Technical + IT, this should feel more implementation-focused and emphasize strongest/recent platforms first.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding proficiency context: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented rather than just a list: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites and modular content builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If this section is meant to stay tool-only, shorten the title to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping platforms here and removing repeated CMS names from the Topline section.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **Front-end implementation:** HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery • **Integrations & tagging:** API integrations, Google Tag Manager • **Edge/serverless & deployment:** Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner.
- Consider changing “Coding & Technical Implementation” to **Development & Technical Implementation** or **Front-End & Integration Tools** for a more senior tone.
- If accurate, add one proof point in recent experience instead of here, e.g., “Delivered front-end implementation, API integrations, and deployment workflows for Drupal-based campaign and search experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills.
- “API integrations” and AI/search-related technical work are also implied in recent project and work-experience entries.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped systems: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the actual mix of platforms.
- Put the strongest, most differentiating tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; de-emphasize generic collaboration tools.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: “used to support cross-team publishing, approvals, and campaign coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools and may add little value unless grouped briefly.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise email operations, this item should signal level of use and avoid repeating “multi-channel communications” already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- If accurate, add scope/context: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise campaign automation)** • **Higher Logic (member communications and newsletters)** • **Mailchimp (email campaign management)**
- Keep naming consistent and concise; consider shortening **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys** to **Dynamics 365 CI/Journeys** if space is tight.
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and strength.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters; don’t restate outcomes here unless you remove them from role entries.
- “Engagement” may feel broad unless supported elsewhere; “member communications” is more specific to this CV.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Tighten it to emphasize platforms over broad concepts, and keep the strongest, most recent analytics stack.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** if you want this section to stay tool-based; keep SEO in competencies instead.
- Remove **Dashboarding**; it’s a capability already implied by Power BI/Looker Studio and better covered in experience/core competencies.
- If space allows, order by strategic weight/recency: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one or making this version tools-only.
- “Dashboarding” and “SEO” are also echoed elsewhere as broader capabilities, so they add little here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational impact, team-building, and distinct early-career contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the second sentence more concrete: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house publishing capacity.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics or metrics if available: event audience size, video cadence, traffic lift, production volume, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten management language: change “providing day-to-day guidance” to “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate,” if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier build/launch phase.
- Website/workflow language also appears in later NACo roles, so keep this entry focused on team formation and hands-on production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells impact. Since later NACo roles already establish digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational achievements—especially the first podcast—without repeating generic content work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific verb and scope, e.g., “produced multimedia and digital content supporting policy communications and organizational programs.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or types/volume of projects supported.
- Keep it to 1–2 lines; this older role should show progression into digital leadership, not compete with recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo entries; keep this item focused on research/innovation support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating “oversaw planning, scripting, and production” if similar production language appears elsewhere; use “launched” and “led end-to-end production” instead.
